doc.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

chapter: Composing and the Thad Jones band
title: The origin of the composition 'Perugia'
summary: Inspired by a hill town in Italy visited with the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band: the evening promenade and the climbing streets.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let me just play something here, to see if you—
Nice chords. What was the inspiration for this particular song. Was there one?

Perugia is a place almost in the center of Italy, and it’s a city on the top of a hill, high on the top of a hill, where the Etruscans, a group of people who escaped from slavery or enslavement in Africa and ran to this area, and stayed there and fought back the Romans and other people by throwing hot oil and rocks and everything else down. Finally the Romans said let them go. Forget them. And they won out. If you read that history, it’s really interesting. And when I got there, knowing nothing about that, I watched these people every day at the top of this hill, and the top of the mountain, with these columns of these buildings and looking like Roman columns, and I said how did they get up there? These people built all this stuff by hand and they walked from one end of the street to the other. And there’s a certain time of day when all the shops close and people just walk promenade. And the introduction that you hear is the promenade [scats] and they’re just trudging and walking back and forth. And here I am in amazement looking at this most amazing thing to see. And then, as I stayed there, I think it was about a week or two, with Thad Jones and Mel Lewis band, and as I stayed there I used to go for long walks and try to walk down the hill on the streets. And you’d walk down a ways and the next thing you know you’re back up on another hill. You’d walk a while then you’d go down this road and it would curve around and you’d be back. There was one way to get down. And you had to go that way to get down off the hill. But any other time you wanted to get down, and you might go down for a ways, but you’d have to end up back on top of the hill. So Perugia was just so beautiful to me. I’d never seen anything like that. And that’s where that melody came from. But it wasn’t an inspiration from Africa, it was more an inspiration from these very, very brown, light skinned but brown skinned people, with the combination of dark eyes and dark features and black hair. Not Sicilians but close. And I’ve never gotten over Perugia. I think if you go there now you might see what I’m talking about because that tradition still goes on, they still walk back and forth in the certain time of the day, everything still closes up and they still walk back and forth like nomads.
